candidates.label: Nea Paphos (Kato Paphos archaeological site)
candidates.support: Nea Paphos, a UNESCO World Heritage archaeological park, was the Roman-period capital of Cyprus and is the undisputed setting of Paul and Barnabas's encounter with the proconsul Sergius Paulus in Acts 13.

summary.text: Paphos (Nea Paphos) was the Roman capital of the province of Cyprus, where Acts records that the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed after witnessing Paul's confrontation with the sorcerer Elymas.

scripture.textWEB: When they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew whose name was Bar Jesus,
Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
